newsitem.title: GERMANY: Issing-Can't say not worried about mark weakness.
newsitem.headline: Issing-Can't say not worried about mark weakness.

text.p: Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing said on Thursday that he could not say he was not concerned about the speed and size of the decline of the deutschemark against the dollar.

In an interview with Germany's N-TV television channel, Issing said: "I am not one of those people who believes he knows what the correct exchange rate is. But that is not to say that I am not worried about the pace and size of the weakening of the mark."
But he added: "It is quite another question what that means for monetary policy."

The mark sank to a six-year low against the dollar on Thursday, trading at one point down to 1.84 marks. By 2028 GMT, however, the German currency had recovered slightly and was trading at 1.83 marks to the dollar.
